_comment: Authoritative project facts: hand-edited, enforced by scripts/check_structure.py (check_H, CONVENTIONS section 15). Choose one frontend stack; list shipped stacks/transports under 'available'.
name: project_keel

template._comment: Keel is a copier template: files suffixed .jinja are rendered, everything else is copied verbatim. `twins` declares every .jinja and what it is FOR, so a new one cannot appear unnoticed — scripts/check_structure.py check_N enforces it, render-free, so it runs in the 3.6 pre-commit gate. 'parity' = must reproduce keel's own file except where templated; 'divergence' = must NOT (the difference is the point); 'generated' = copier writes it into a new project and keel commits none of its own. A generated project has no .jinja files, so check_N is silent there.

structure._comment: Top-level directories this project adds beyond the CONVENTIONS section 2 taxonomy, by name. scripts/check_structure.py check_B errors on any other non-hidden top-level directory, on a name here that does not exist or is already in the taxonomy, and on a declared directory without README.md and CLAUDE.md. Names only: the directory's own README.md summary says why it exists.

make_targets._comment: Every annotated make target opens its `## ` help with an effect label from the closed vocabulary [local] [tree] [read] [cost] [write] (docs/adr/0011-make-target-effect-labels.md). scripts/check_structure.py check_W validates this block and the labels; scripts/run_make_target.py runs only a target whose label falls inside gate_effects, sets gate_runner_var=1 last so WRITE_GUARD refuses a [write] target, accepts only the gate_vars as NAME=VALUE variables (each value one path-like word), and fails a run that changed what git sees. unattended_vars are the variables WRITE_GUARD refuses under; write_shapes are target-name suffixes that must be [write]; area_dir is the directory of <area>.mk makefiles (null: areas off); effect_proof_skip keeps a [local] target out of tests/integration/test_make_target_effects.py, by name and reason only.

effect_proof_skip.new: generates a project outside the tree and needs DEST and a clean checkout
effect_proof_skip.run: starts the app composition root, which serves until stopped
effect_proof_skip.smoke: selects no tests today, and pytest exits 5 on an empty selection
effect_proof_skip.run-api: a dev server that never exits
effect_proof_skip.run-web: a dev server that never exits and needs npm
effect_proof_skip.test: runs the whole suite, which holds this sweep, so it would run itself; tests/integration/test_write_guard.py runs its make-driving cases through the gate runner
effect_proof_skip.integration: runs the integration suite, which holds this proof

child_env._comment: The environment a process keel's code starts inherits (docs/adr/0012-child-process-environment-allowlist.md). scripts/child_env.py build_child_env starts from an empty dict and copies only these names, a name starting with a prefix, make_targets.unattended_vars and gate_vars (so WRITE_GUARD and the interpreter choice survive a hop through a Python doer), and, for a model adapter, its models.credential_env names; scripts/check_structure.py check_X holds every spawn to it. Why each family: PATH, HOME, USER and LOGNAME to find and run tools; LANG, LANGUAGE, TERM, TZ and LC_ for locale and output; the proxy and CA-bundle names because this network intercepts TLS; GIT_CONFIG_* so the test suite's hermetic git reaches git, and GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE and the object-directory names so a git hook's child sees the repository git ran it in; TEMP, TMP and TMPDIR for scratch; VIRTUAL_ENV and XDG_* for tool caches; SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for reproducible output. Deliberately absent: every credential (a model adapter's go in models.credential_env), MAKEFLAGS, MFLAGS, MAKELEVEL, MAKEOVERRIDES and MAKEFILES (a nested make must not inherit the outer make's goals; check_X refuses them here), PYTHONPATH (a caller passes it in extra), and GIT_ as a prefix (it would admit GIT_ASKPASS and GIT_SSH_COMMAND). Defence-in-depth, not a sandbox: a same-uid child can still read /proc/$PPID/environ.

models._comment: Model/provider adapters this project makes available (registered in models/registry.py). 'default' is the registry default; the showcase surfaces this list. credential_env names, per adapter that starts a process, the environment variables that process needs on top of child_env (scripts/child_env.py build_child_env(credentials_for=<adapter>)); an adapter absent from it gets the base allowlist only. Add a name here, not in code, when a CLI needs one more (for example a cloud provider's region).

practices._comment: Domain coding-practice profiles are DEFINED in config/practices.json (ai/cuda/langgraph) and ENABLED here — flip a flag to true to turn its domain checks on (e.g. cuda -> check_L naked-tensor, resource-context-manager advisory). All off keeps the template domain-neutral. Validated by check_structure.py (check_H); consumed by check_L and check_practices.py.
